claims.text: Equiatomic noble-metal HEA nanoparticles will form a uniform single-phase FCC structure under the specified synthesis conditions.
Maximized mixing entropy is responsible for formation of the uniform single-phase FCC structure.
A uniform single-phase FCC structure produces an ensemble of optimized catalytic active sites.
Deviating from equiatomic composition will induce phase segregation or elemental clustering.
Phase segregation or elemental clustering caused by non-equiatomic composition will produce poorer catalytic performance.
The controlled comparison will reduce the atomic fraction of one element relative to an equiatomic baseline.
Degree of atomic-level mixing can be assessed from elemental homogeneity and the presence of a single FCC phase versus segregation or clustering.
High mixing entropy in equiatomic alloys counteracts positive mixing enthalpy.
Counteracting positive mixing enthalpy favors a homogeneous solid solution.
A homogeneous solid solution exposes a balanced ensemble of catalytic active sites.
Non-equiatomic composition can create defective surfaces or secondary-phase boundaries.
Defective surfaces or secondary-phase boundaries impair catalytic performance.
Equiatomic nanoparticles will have more uniform crystallite sizes than non-equiatomic nanoparticles.
Equiatomic nanoparticles will have a more homogeneous elemental distribution than non-equiatomic nanoparticles.
Equiatomic nanoparticles will show more stable and higher-turnover oxygen-reduction catalysis than non-equiatomic nanoparticles.
Within the nanoscale regime, mixing-entropy effects dominate reliable material formation.
Composition-induced electronic-structure or surface-chemistry changes may independently affect catalytic performance.
